blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — YESCARTA cytokine release syndrome recognition
stem: Several days after receiving axicabtagene ciloleucel (YESCARTA), a client develops fever, hypotension, and new hypoxia. Which nursing interpretation is most appropriate?

options.A: Suspect cytokine release syndrome, urgently escalate care, evaluate other causes of fever, hypotension, and hypoxia, and prepare for severity-based treatment such as tocilizumab with or without corticosteroids.
options.B: Treat the findings as a benign expected effect of CAR-T therapy because fever with hypotension and hypoxia does not require urgent reassessment or enhanced monitoring.
options.C: Interpret the findings as proof that CAR-T treatment has failed because cytokine release syndrome reflects absent therapeutic immune activation rather than treatment toxicity.
options.D: Assume infection explains the entire presentation and exclude CAR-T toxicity before evaluating the client for cytokine release syndrome or other treatment-related causes.

rationale: Current YESCARTA labeling identifies fever, hypotension, and hypoxia as characteristic CRS manifestations. Clinicians should identify CRS from the presentation while evaluating and treating other causes of fever, hypoxia, and hypotension. Grade 2 or higher CRS requires enhanced monitoring, and tocilizumab with or without corticosteroids is used according to severity. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize fever, hypotension, and hypoxia after YESCARTA as possible CRS requiring urgent assessment, alternative-cause evaluation, and severity-based treatment preparation.
source_version_date: Current DailyMed label published June 2026; accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: §2.3 Management of Severe Adverse Reactions and §5.1 CRS: identify CRS clinically; evaluate/treat other causes of fever, hypoxia, hypotension; Grade ≥2 enhanced monitoring; tocilizumab and corticosteroids per severity.
source_claim_supported: Post-YESCARTA fever, hypotension, and hypoxia may represent CRS; evaluate alternatives and manage urgently with severity-based monitoring and anti-CRS therapy.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: recognize severe biologic/cellular-therapy toxicity, differentiate competing causes, monitor urgently, and prepare rescue therapy.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Removed absolute-word cues and rewrote all options as full competing interpretations of the same post-CAR-T presentation.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches current YESCARTA CRS guidance; no residual absolute cue or second defensible interpretation remains.
